selection.rule: STUDY v0.8 section 8: frozen headline-cost (H) front after Chang's filter; step envelope on G = {100k,200k,300k,350k,400k,450k} H; D_screen from CH-8 alone on validation (8.2; empty D_screen gives INCOMPLETE and Kai decides before S3/S4); form rule 8.3; coverage-first BEST 8.4; under option (b) of 19.2 item 12, g* = the smallest g in D_screen such that at every g' in D_screen with g' >= g BEST is feasible in all three screen seeds and its mean paired validation top-1 gain over CH-8 is > 0, frozen in S2 (none gives an empty band); PID selection (8.6): the checkpoint with the highest validation top-1 among those with frozen H <= 350,000 passing Chang's filter, ties as 8.1, never the closest over-budget point; structure record at every frozen checkpoint (8.1): degenerate Q, K, V, O or FFN contraction, binary or HGQ, defined by effect (zero variance over the validation jets after the output quantizer) with route, zero columns by route, zero-width input fractions, per-head softmax zero-width fractions

screen.interval_method: screen: ordinary 95 percent paired t over seeds (df = 2), descriptive only, with sign counts and a paired jet bootstrap beside; per-seed Pareto dominance and 2^3 factorial main effects and interactions descriptive on validation (S2) and held-out (after the freeze); no verdict labels at n = 3. S2 validation outputs for Kai's S4 decision: per option the threshold in observed s_d, the section-6 table power, and the plug-in joint power at BEST's observed per-g validation gains and s_d (section-6 model, rho 0 and 0.9) with the smallest single-allowance power beside, both also with sigma_d set to 6.28 x the observed s_d at each g (upper 95 percent bound of sigma_d/s_d at df = 2), labelled optimistic (selected on these seeds), with the runner-up beside and the count of g with gain <= 0 or BEST infeasible; the same at the pooled sigma-hat_d (two-way arm x seed table of validation top-1 per g over CH-8 and the chosen-form cells, residual df = 2(rows - 1), 16 with nine rows) and its upper chi-square bound; the null selection reference for BEST's gain (median and 95th percentile under zero true gains, simulated with the section 8.3-8.4 rules); the number of distinct checkpoint pairs behind the allowances per seed. Factorial effects also with randomized-block intervals (seed as block, df = 14) and the additive-model cell beside BEST. All descriptive; they enter no rule. Claims only in confirmation_stage.

claim.status: requires Kai's budget approval beyond the 400 GPU-h cap and his choice of option (STUDY v0.8 section 19.2 item 11); decided after S2 validation outputs and before any held-out read. This object is option A as adopted (seeds 4-8, ramp and PID, 20 arms). Option B: the same four groups on seeds 4-11 (32 arms). Option C: CH-8-C and BEST-C on seeds 4-11, no PID arms (16 arms), C2 alone at alpha = 0.05, or sharing alpha with the ramp point claim C3r under option (c) of 19.2 item 12. The claim domain D_C2 is fixed by Kai before any launch (19.2 item 12): D_band = {g in D_conf : g >= g*} under option (b), the recommended default, or D_conf under option (a). The claim-scope protocol file frozen before any S4 launch is regenerated for the chosen option and claim domain.

claim.interval_method: paired t over seeds (df = n - 1). C2 intersection-union test over D_C2: at every g in D_C2, two-sided interval at level L, lower bound > 0 for ABOVE ON GRID; under option (b) the same test over all of D_conf is reported beside as the nested strong form, adding no alpha. L = 1 - 0.05/2 when C2 shares alpha = 0.05 with C3 (options A, B) or with C3r (option C with option (c)); 0.95 for C2 alone (option C). C3 PID and C3r ramp-350k: same level. Variant offered to Kai under option (c), not the default: when 350,000 is in D_C2, C3r's null implies C2's null, so C3r could be tested at C2's own level with no added alpha (C2 at 0.95 and 0.836 s_d under option C); it applies only if 350,000 is in D_C2, fixed on validation before the held-out read; the pre-registered default remains the Bonferroni split. Descriptive CROSSING/LOCAL labels: simultaneous Bonferroni over 7 contrasts (6 grid + PID) or 6 (option C). C4 firmware dominance (only where C2 is ABOVE ON GRID): per g in D_C2 the level-L paired t interval on LUT_BEST - LUT_CH-8 at one part, stage and settings; LUT ADVANTAGE if upper bound < 0, NOT A LUT ADVANTAGE if lower bound >= 0, else UNRESOLVED; supported only with LUT ADVANTAGE and a post-trace accuracy lower bound > 0 at every g in D_C2. C6 (secondary): ordinary 95 percent paired t intervals for the mean ablation, the static-attention ablation (per-(head, query, key) validation-mean probabilities after the softmax output quantizer, the mean accumulated in float64 and cast back) and the zero-logit ablation (logits 0 through the model's own QSoftmax), all > 0; entropy of row-renormalized post-quantizer probabilities < log 8 in every seed (consistency check); no degenerate K, V or O by effect; a degenerate Q gives 'used, with input-independent queries', or 'used, as query-independent attention pooling' where Q_t is identical across query positions; a Q equal to 0 at every element is reported as for a degenerate K ('input-independent attention weights'), with no change to any C6 outcome (its logits are 0, so the static-attention ablation is 0); beside each ablation, the count of validation entries where a downstream datalane WRAP quantizer receives a value outside its (k, i, f) range (O's input quantizer for the static and zero-logit ablations, the second tanh table's input quantizer for the mean ablation), with the unablated model's count as baseline and the label 'overflow-affected' when nonzero, and for the entropy the rows with any negative post-quantizer entry counted separately; the C6 rule is unchanged and a C6 statement resting on an overflow-affected ablation carries the label; reported per g, overall at every g in D_C2.
